Bare Necessities: 2027 Go Play 17DBS Sport Might Be the Best Deal for Big Families and New RV Owners
21 photos
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot
A recent study completed by RVIA mentions that Americans are still placing affordability above all other RV and camper traits. So, with that in mind, I've decided to bring to light a camper that gives American families all they need and nothing else, and all at a price that really surprised me.
Folks, Wayfinder RV showcases a starting price tag of just $17,500 for the 2027 Go Play 17DBS Sport, this brands latest and most-equipped layout that’s aimed at the entry level RV owner, and if I may, I was actually blown away with the number of features that this brand managed to stuff into the trailer.
As mentioned, this is an entry level unit and for the price tag that it carries, we’re looking at a “stick and tin” construction with a wooden frame and painted aluminum exterior. While it’s not the sort of construction that’ll last you ages, with proper love and care, some can see up to 15 years of use.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot While it may not be the most feature-filled option on the market, nor one that calls upon the most prime of materials, it does offer ample space for larger families to get out there and, well, “Go Play,” in particular, outside, as there isn’t much to do inside but sleep, lounge around, cook and eat, and escape bad weather.
For a general feeling of the layout, allow me to point out that at the very front of the unit, Wayfinder decided to add a residential 60x80-inch queen mattress with storage options underneath and above. The AC hovers above and sticks out into the interior, so watch your head.
This is where two people will be able to rest their heads at night, maybe even three if a small child is in there, and another two kids or adults will be catching Zs on the modular U-shaped dinette. That’s four to five guests so far and while most people would feel that this is about the limit in this price bracket, it isn’t, with Wayfinder stuffing two double bunks into the rear of the 17DBS.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot Josh, the host in the video below does point out a peak of 600 lbs (272 kg) per bunk. Plen-ty and quite the sleeping capacity for something that costs as much as some teardrop campers I've written about this year, and there’s still a bit more to go over.
Since this isn’t the biggest camper in the world, rolling in with a length of a bit over 23.5 ft (7.2 m), and most of the space inside is occupied by the beds, it leaves little room for a complete bathroom or massive kitchen where you can cook up a storm .
For example, the bathroom, while completed with a separate toilet and shower, doesn’t include a sink, so you’ll have to wash your hands elsewhere, nor does it include a powered vent, so you’ll need to be sure to air things out very well or go for an upgrade.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot As for the kitchen, it’s there, and ready with a fridge that’s decently sized for a group this large, doesn’t include much countertop space to work with for meal preps. You'll need to use a sink cover to do so as the cooktops do stick out of the countertop. There’s a microwave inside too.
Our stays are also supported with features like a tankless water heater, 19K BTU furnace, the AC I mentioned, ample lighting, and 30 gals of freshwater. Do keep in mind that this makes up for a camper that weighs 4,800 lbs (2,177 kg) GVWR, so be sure your vehicle can tow this much. Some SUVs can, placing this RV option on the radar of vehicle owners that don’t just have trucks.
Cargo-carrying capacity does stand at nearly 1,070 lbs (485 kg), but if you add any upgrades, you’ll start to diminish that number for toys, gear, and other essentials.
Now, I stumbled across this unit in a video from Josh the RV Nerd at Bish’s RV (Hat-tip to you folks!) and in it, he does showcase what this camper’s “road mode” is like. If I may, I was surprised to see that we can access every single space inside this one while it’s scrunched up for the road.
Photo: Josh the RV Nerd at Bish's RV | YouTube Screenshot The bunks can be accessed, the bedroom too, the bathroom, and you can still whip up a sandwich or grab a change of clothes. What you can’t do, according to Josh, is use the dinette be it for sitting, sleeping, or “human bouncing.” The dinette cushions also don’t have a particular way to keep them in place and not bounce around while you drive.
What I'd personally like to point out is that the spec sheet mentions that solar is NA, so you’ll clearly need to go the full mile in terms of upgrades and gear to tap into free power, or optionally, you can opt for a portable power station with internal inverter and a set of solar panels. Some dealers will install solar for you, for an extra buck, of course.
Oh, and last but not least, keep in mind that some dealers are selling this a bit under the MSRP, sometimes, adding a minor upgrade or two here and there, so take the time to shop around, not to mention making then ‘fight’ over your money; disrupt the system.
Frankly, it appears as though Wayfinder is about to sell some 2027 Go Play 17DBS Sport travel trailers.
